scope: CVG-002 bounded one-active-encounter-per-account-patient invariant and stable conflict mapping

criteria.description: The canonical additive migration fails closed on historical active duplicates, rejects an incompatible same-name index, and creates a valid partial unique index on account and patient for non-closed encounters.
criteria.limitations: The migration does not remediate existing duplicates; a human-approved data task is required before applying it to an environment containing them.

criteria.description: Only the named PostgreSQL active-encounter unique violation is translated to ConflictError, while unrelated errors and tenant checks remain preserved across create, update and reopen persistence paths.
criteria.limitations: The proof is local and disposable; target driver, deployed role and network behavior remain outside this gate.

criteria.description: Independent database-backed runtimes serialize concurrent opens, preserve account scope, allow a new encounter after close, and reject reopening when another active encounter exists.
criteria.limitations: Separate patient records are used for separate accounts because the existing composite patient/account foreign key rejects reuse of one global patient UUID across accounts.

criteria.description: The authoritative API path exposes database-origin active-encounter conflicts as HTTP 409 and restores speculative queue state when persistence fails.
criteria.limitations: The HTTP proof is compiled and local; it does not certify a multi-process deployed cluster or external queue/cache behavior.

criteria.description: Focused tests, full workspace tests, build, typecheck, coverage, security and static contract rails pass after the implementation.
criteria.limitations: Remote CI, browser acceptance for this slice, target operations, providers and release acceptance remain outside the bounded test rails.

criteria.description: A fresh independent read-only review found no Critical or High issue in the bounded implementation; its Medium findings were remediated and the remaining low-level limitations stay explicit.
criteria.limitations: A separate reviewer-role attempt was unavailable because the account model policy rejected the requested model; it is not approval. Low-level test-pool/session portability remains bounded evidence debt.

criteria.description: The bounded clinical result is reconciled without promoting the parent CVG-002, strict Vetus parity, clinical parity, enterprise readiness or release gate.
criteria.limitations: General parity remains 98/100 with 4/11 verified, clinical parity 100/100 with 2/3 verified, and enterprise readiness 95/100 with 42 PASS / 3 WARN / 1 FAIL.

gaps: Historical duplicate rows require a separately authorized remediation task; this gate never deletes, closes, merges or rewrites them.
The existing composite patient/account foreign key prevents one global patient UUID from being reused across accounts; cross-account proof uses separate patient records.
Local PostgreSQL does not certify target TCP/RLS/roles, deployed replicas, Redis/cache behavior, providers, production, recovery, remote CI or release acceptance.
The independent review is conditional and a second requested reviewer role was unavailable; no unconditional post-fix approval is inferred.
Full encounter transaction atomicity and broader ERP/Vetus readiness remain outside this bounded task.
conditions: Keep this result limited to the canonical active encounter uniqueness invariant and its conflict boundary.
Remediate or explicitly accept historical duplicates through a separate human-approved task before applying migration 0151 to an affected environment.
Revalidate before changing encounter lifecycle semantics, patient/account keys, queue ordering, target roles/RLS, providers, production, deployment or release scope.

authority.actor: Ricardo (repository owner), via the original consolidation brief
authority.scope: CVG-002 bounded active-encounter uniqueness and conflict mapping
authority.decision: Authorize reversible repository implementation, one additive canonical packages/db migration, focused API/domain tests and disposable PostgreSQL concurrency verification for the invariant that a tenant patient has at most one non-closed encounter. Exclude historical duplicate remediation, provider, credentials, target, production, deployment, external mutation and release acceptance.
authority.expires_or_revalidates: Revalidate before historical data remediation, another encounter transaction family, target operation, provider, credential, production, deployment or release action.

next_action: Keep parent CVG-002 and the global program IN_PROGRESS/PARTIAL; preserve target/provider/operations/parity/readiness/release gaps and revalidate this bounded gate on the listed triggers.
revalidation_triggers: Changes to encounter status semantics, patient/account foreign keys, migration source or migration checksums
Changes to queue association ordering, repository error mapping, reopen timeline behavior or distributed cache behavior
Applying migration 0151 to an environment with historical duplicate active encounters
Changes to target roles/RLS, providers, credentials, production, deployment or release scope
